text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka, has sent to the Croatian deputy foreign minister, Ivo Sanader, a draft of a statement which will be adopted at next meeting of Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and chairman of Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic.
- Sanader has protested to Sarajevo over alleged anti-Croatian media campaign in the Bosnian press and over statements by Bosnian state officials.
- General manager of Croatian railways, Marijan Klaric, said railway traffic between Bosnia and Croatia will resume in September.
- The federation minister of energy, mining and industry, Izudin Kapetanovic, requests that Slovenia, Austria, Italy and Germany issue long-term visas for truck drivers transporting Bosnian exports.

- Sulejman Ugljanin, president of the Moslem National Council in the town of Novi Pazar in neighbouring Yugoslavia, says the Serbian police force are establishing a police dictatorship in Novi Pazar and Sandzak. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
